prompt: In triangle $ABC$, angle $A = 30^\circ$ and angle $B = 90^\circ$. Side $b$ (the side across from $B$) is $10$. Find side $a$, the side across from $A$.
hint: You have a matching pair (side $b$ with angle $B$), so reach for the Law of Sines.

hints.text: You have a matching pair (side $b$ with angle $B$), so reach for the Law of Sines.
Set up $\frac{a}{\sin A} = \frac{b}{\sin B}$, which is $\frac{a}{\sin 30^\circ} = \frac{10}{\sin 90^\circ}$.

explanation: The Law of Sines pairs each side with the angle ACROSS from it.
Since $\sin 90^\circ = 1$, the right side is just $10$.

alternativeExplanations.title: A table of the two pairs
steps: Make two columns: ANGLE and SIDE ACROSS FROM IT.
Row 1: angle 30°, side a. Row 2: angle 90°, side 10.
The Law of Sines says both rows give the same ratio: a ÷ 0.5 must equal 10 ÷ 1 = 10, so a = 5.

alternativeExplanations.title: Picture the half-equilateral
steps: A 30-60-90 triangle is an equilateral triangle sliced straight down the middle.
The side across the 90° corner is the long slanted side; the side across the 30° corner is the short one.
In that sliced triangle the short side is exactly half the long one: half of 10 is 5.
